ai.description: Beddome's Cat Skink reaches 6 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe and pale spots. Key features include a short, rounded snout and small, widely separated limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ristella beddomii* is distinguished by having only three fingers on its forelimbs, whereas other *Ristella* species possess four.
ai.habitat: *Ristella beddomii* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ristella beddomii* is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts small insects among leaf litter, often using its agile movements to quickly retreat into cover when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ristella beddomii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ristella beddomii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
